survey: A traditional straw broom shown on its own at a diagonal against a wavy blue background. The straight, round wooden handle runs from upper right to lower left and ends in a rounded knob cap at the top. At the lower end the handle goes into a tight straw collar. That collar is bound with two or three red cord wraps that sit flush around the neck. Below the binding the straw bristles fan out into a bell-shaped head, and the uneven tips end in a ragged, clumped edge, as real straw does. The broom floats with no ground plane, which is normal for a single-item icon card, so it is not a support error. The handle stays straight and evenly thick, the bristles hang from the bound neck, and nothing passes through anything else. The broom could clearly sweep. The red wraps are drawn as neat rings with no visible cord ends. That is a normal simplification of a binding, not a loose end.
